rail_guard.text: Bushmills Station, home of the little steam railway to the Causeway. Narrow gauge, big smile, and a chimney that thinks it's a volcano.
Hop aboard. The Wildlore rail runs to any town you have visited on this island. Where to?

mill_keeper.text: Don't tell anyone, but the mill hasn't ground a grain in a century. The wheel still turns, though, for the tourists. It likes the audience.
The Bush is a quick little river. Quick to flood, quick to clear. Like a Bushmills argument.

green_gardener.text: I do the flower beds on the green. Two hundred years of Bushmills folk have walked across them, and not one asked permission.
Planting tulips is an act of faith. You bury a thing in the cold, in the dark, and trust it to come back with a better attitude.

station_volunteer.text: We run a little steam train from here to the Causeway. Two kilometres, three-foot gauge, and a driver who waves at sheep.
It's a slow train. That's the point. If you wanted to arrive quickly, you wouldn't be going to the Causeway.

young_cyclist.text: I've cycled the whole coast road to get here and I'm thrilled. My legs have asked me to stop saying thrilled.
There's a great chippy by the green. It's called the Chippy. Subtle, but it works.

post_clerk.text: Letters, parcels and gossip. Two out of three are free of charge.
I know everybody who lives here and which dog belongs to whom. It's the dogs I rely on. They're never wrong.
